features.title: Everything you need for a convincing 3D packaging preview
features.intro: Whether you call it a 3D box simulator, carton configurator, or structural packaging preview, these tools help you validate scale, readability, and shelf presence before you commit to plates or samples.
features.viewportBody: Orbit, zoom (scroll or slider), HDRI environments, shadows, and optional grid—ideal for packaging reviews and client sign-off.
features.dimensionsBody: Set width, height, and depth in millimeters, centimeters, or inches. Scene units convert to centimeters for consistent 3D scale.
features.materialsBody: Kraft, white carton, gloss or matte plastic, corrugated, and metallic foil—roughness, clearcoat, and environment response tuned for packaging looks.
features.openingsBody: Closed view, lid from back, split top flaps (hinge on long or short side), and a swinging door-style left panel—animated open amount.
features.artworkBody: Upload PNG or JPG per face, rotate in 90° steps, and apply one image to all faces when you need a quick placeholder wrap.
features.envBody: Choose from studio, city, warehouse, sunset, and dawn environments. This is a great way to get feedback on your design.
features.cloudBody: Use File → Save or Save As to upload your design. Get an editor link for yourself and a separate view-only preview link for clients—artwork and settings included.
features.previewBody: Share a presentation link that opens the studio in read-only mode. Clients can orbit, zoom, adjust lighting, and export PNGs—without changing dimensions, artwork, or saving over your work.
features.jsonBody: Download a v1 JSON backup with dimensions, materials, openings, and embedded images—or import a file to restore the full scene offline.
features.pngBody: Export a high-resolution PNG snapshot of the live viewport for decks, RFQs, and marketing—alongside cloud share links for interactive review.
features.recordBody: Record a 15-second video of the viewport, then download the MP4 file. This is a great way to share your 3D packaging simulator with your team or clients.

quote.text: The goal is not to replace die-line CAD—it is to give everyone in the room a shared, believable picture of the box before time and money disappear into the wrong structure.

what-is-3d-box-designer.question: What is a 3D box designer or packaging simulator?
what-is-3d-box-designer.answer: A 3D box designer lets you preview how flat packaging artwork and structural choices look on a three-dimensional carton or mailer. A packaging simulator applies realistic lighting and materials so stakeholders can review proportions, openings, and branding before print.

free-3d-box-maker.question: Is 3D Box Studio a free 3D box maker?
free-3d-box-maker.answer: Yes. 3D Box Studio is a free 3D box maker and design tool that runs entirely in your browser. There is no paywall for dimensions, materials, openings, per-face artwork, HDRI lighting, PNG export, or JSON import/export. Create a free account to open the studio and start designing. Email verification is optional for now—you can save, share, and export right after signing up.

3d-box-simulation-use.question: What is 3D box simulation used for?
3d-box-simulation-use.answer: 3D box simulation helps packaging designers, brand teams, and printers validate scale, graphic placement, and opening behavior before committing to plates or physical samples. It is ideal for client presentations, e-commerce mockups, and internal design reviews—not for engineering production die-lines.

vs-esko-artioscad.question: Is this a substitute for Esko, ArtiosCAD, or dedicated packaging CAD?
vs-esko-artioscad.answer: No. Those platforms engineer production die-lines. This 3D packaging simulator helps you communicate look and feel, camera angles, and rough scale early. Export is a viewport PNG, not a print plate.

vs-mockup-templates.question: How is a 3D box design maker different from a mockup template site?
vs-mockup-templates.answer: Template libraries give you fixed box shapes with uploaded artwork. A 3D box design maker like 3D Box Studio lets you adjust width, height, depth, materials, lid and flap openings, and per-face graphics in one interactive viewport—better for custom carton sizes and structural previews.

mobile-support.question: Does the 3D box simulator work on mobile?
mobile-support.answer: The studio is built for desktop browsers with WebGL. Phones may run it, but the control density is optimized for keyboard and mouse users.

data-storage.question: Where is my data stored?
data-storage.answer: While you work, your design stays in the browser session. When you upload face artwork, the studio auto-saves to the cloud as “Untitled” (rename anytime via File → Rename). Images upload to AWS S3 and configuration is stored in a Postgres database. You can also save manually with File → Save (⌘S).

cloud-share.question: How do cloud save and share links work?
cloud-share.answer: Uploading face artwork auto-saves your design to the cloud as “Untitled”. Use File → Rename to change the name. File → Save (⌘S) updates an existing project; File → Save As creates a copy with a new link. File → Open lets you paste a share link or ID to reload a saved design. After saving, use File → Share Preview Link or Copy Preview Link to send clients a separate view-only URL (/preview/…). Editor links use /studio/… and are not exposed in preview mode.
